## Design

### 2026-10-30: This session, I spent my time coming up with ideas and doing a bunch of research into what I actually wanted to do. At first, I thought of using an oled, but thats too boring so instead, I decided to

**2h**

This session, I spent my time coming up with ideas and doing a bunch of research into what I actually wanted to do. At first, I thought of using an oled, but thats too boring so instead, I decided to go with a TFT, a 2.8" one.
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/6NsErT1120V2FDTcxwPhvTmpArnC2ArA/db779ae8607074d4e570618038d041a0f8552888ff96540421827f29c27478ac.png)
It has touch on it and it has color and a bigger screen, so that's pretty cool. I had to look at prices for different models, which is how I came up with the 2.8" as its pretty cheap. I chose a raspberry pi pico as the controller as its cheap and has a bunch of gpios.

But I also wanted some other way to input, and I thought of Capacitative touch. But after some research, I found out it wasn't practical with a raspberry pi pico as you needed a bunch of 1M Ohm resistors. So instead, I decided to use some cherry MX switches from my previous project since I had some left over.
I also had to find footprints and 3d models for the TFT. After a bunch of searching, I came out unsuccessful. So i decided to look for the dimensions instead and use a pin footprint instead of an actual screen footprint. After a lot of searching, I found the dimensions on a random amazon listing.
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/6NsErT1120V2FDTcxwPhvTmpArnC2ArA/a44766c1d743a603f169da5aa6c4c0cea37c39998e8cc5428ec6d8e901988563.png)

Next, I have to actually make the schematic and stuff, which I'll have to do a bunch of research for finding out how to wire the screen.

### 2026-10-30: This session, I made the schematic, and made the PCB but I havent routed it yet. The reason this took so long was because I didn't know how to wire the screen.

**5h**

This session, I made the schematic, and made the PCB but I havent routed it yet. The reason this took so long was because I didn't know how to wire the screen.
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/6NsErT1120V2FDTcxwPhvTmpArnC2ArA/c741dc9113c841823ce0d1356c1f27793d4d13c9fb0afa92d39ef3ddf078b4fa.png)
I searched around on the internet, tried to get AIs help, but none of those worked for finding the right keymappings. But then I came across a random youtube tutorial that had some wiring to an ESP32 devkit, so i took inspiration from that.
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/6NsErT1120V2FDTcxwPhvTmpArnC2ArA/b4291b7b3b0893d94692184284c3c3088359ffaaf6497b0bee8827497516e2c3.png)
After some schematic making and a looot of trouble shooting, I was able to get it to 0 errors and 0 warnings, which was huge.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/6NsErT1120V2FDTcxwPhvTmpArnC2ArA/a54f4d1ef1476de94ca8cca3ce99b144453b5f1f25fa1600237888816225cea1.png)
Next I started on the PCB. Since I didn't have a footprint for the TFT, I used measurements I found earlier to make a silkscreen outline for it.
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/6NsErT1120V2FDTcxwPhvTmpArnC2ArA/550dc4776985c18c1fda8284beee66c1a9b401b5c9558af7d3cf9724520395f6.png)
Getting the general arrangments of the parts on the PCB was fine, but routing was reaaaally frustrating. I tried for so long, but I just couldn't find the right arrangement. I'll leave that for next session. This is what I'm up to now:
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/6NsErT1120V2FDTcxwPhvTmpArnC2ArA/b53df282a538c273653b954f0b317ee2b913d7e6a30913ada2f21709c55537c7.png)
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/6NsErT1120V2FDTcxwPhvTmpArnC2ArA/8e15d706c355768e79093d73d544236a7eb75cb4329a9ee616c93936f0aa2c78.png)

### 2026-10-31: Routing the PCB this session was super frustrating, mainly because of my lack of knowledge. I spent more than an hour trying to do it only on the F.Cu, and I didn't know you could use the B.Cu too. I

**2h**

Routing the PCB this session was super frustrating, mainly because of my lack of knowledge. I spent more than an hour trying to do it only on the F.Cu, and I didn't know you could use the B.Cu too. I was able to do it with both layers, but then with 2 routes left, I just couldn't find a way to do it. That's when I realized vias existed, so I was able to fix that too. Would've been nice to know, but at least I learned something.
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/6NsErT1120V2FDTcxwPhvTmpArnC2ArA/2808bb402edf4c7ca8f7a6a1ae98eac0b3b666e4b27e8b9da97536c69c395818.png)
So now I have 2 vias, and the whole board is routed. It definitely isn't the prettiest, but it'll do. This is my final PCB, and then I'm gonna be moving onto firmware.
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/6NsErT1120V2FDTcxwPhvTmpArnC2ArA/c3c7050fe586da2774e323130e531ec93d4083c0fa762c400ebcf7724b1a172f.png)

### 2026-10-31: I got some firmware for the project this session. I had to download a driver library that I'll need to import on to the pico when i get it.

**2h**

I got some firmware for the project this session. I had to download a driver library that I'll need to import on to the pico when i get it.
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/6NsErT1120V2FDTcxwPhvTmpArnC2ArA/7d321c581a128fbd893e899ce8995864924c2e45e6b349bff502e969b0cb4011.png).
Then I made some temporary placeholder code for the screen.  It displays 6 counters of different colors on the screen, and every time u press one of the 6 buttons on the mini console or whatever, it's respective counter goes up by 1. It took a while since I don't just want it to keep adding one  when the button was held down. I had to figure out what libraries and stuff to get, and once I did, I got to coding. I'm not very good at this so it took me a while, and its not the most efficient code, but hey, it should work. I did a lot of research, and I did use AI to help, but it didn't code, i just asked it how to do stuff and the code's formatting (I suck at coding). Eventually though, I got to this, I don't even know if it works cuz I can't test it out, but we'll see. Its 150 lines of code, and these are the first 50 lines:
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/6NsErT1120V2FDTcxwPhvTmpArnC2ArA/bd701d09ca3770387580bd8d53a7d1fb76959d95d55dffea73743efa999eb644.png)
I'm honestly surprised it only took me 2 hours, and now I'm basically done with this week's project. Just gotta fill in the BOM and the repo and I'll be good to go.
